pr_title: If oaep_md is not initialized, correctly initialize it
pr_body:
Fixes #20993

<!--

If this fixes a GitHub issue, make sure to have a line saying 'Fixes #XXXX' (without quotes) in the commit message.

<!-- Remove items that do not apply. For completed items, change [ ] to [x]. -->

- [ ] tests are added or updated
pr_comments: I've set tests: exempted but it should be quite easy to add one I think.
Not so sure about providing the test as there is no way to set oaep_md to NULL
Adjusted a commit message, don't think any reconfirmations needed.

> Not so sure about providing the test as there is no way to set oaep_md to NULL

Isn't it NULL when the context is initialized?

> > Not so sure about providing the test as there is no way to set oaep_md to NULL
> 
> Isn't it NULL when the context is initialized?

It is - but set to SHA1 as soon as we set OAEP padding
Hmm... then it is actually unreachable?
Yes, and that's why it was not found until I started implementing some Red Hat patch.
Hmm... thinking about it... the initialization when setting the pad mode doesn't make sense to me. What if you want to use some provider that does not implement SHA1 and you want OAEP with SHA256 md?
And there are more issues - mdprops is ignored here.

> Hmm... thinking about it... the initialization when setting the pad mode doesn't make sense to me. What if you want to use some provider that does not implement SHA1 and you want OAEP with SHA256 md?

Then you provide it via the `digest` param

> And there are more issues - mdprops is ignored here.

It's a consistent approach for both fips and default provider there.

24 hours has passed since 'approval: done' was set, but as this PR has been updated in that time the label 'approval: ready to merge' is not being automatically set.  Please review the updates and set the label manually.

What are the steps forward from here?

The code is obviously wrong, and my patch fixes it.
I agree that we could fix it better fetching a digest using props. Do we want it to be a part of this PR or not?

What you have done is fine..
I assume we added this code so that by default, old code just worked as it did before.
I was suggesting that if you hit this path in your app, then you are probably better off using setparams instead..
Currently in setparams we allow propq to be set if you set the digest, which is good enough.

The code is basically unreachable and was reached by me by accident. This snippet is definitely wrong, BTW, and deserves a fix. Do we want a complete fix here (e.g. proper fetching props) is a separate question.
Merged to master, 3.1, and 3.0 branches. Thank you.
